summary: Wenatchee NF summit above Lake Wenatchee: a 1914 camp, a 1920 cupola, disputed 1933 and 1957 cabs; cab burned in 1975. WTA says the trail was closed in July 2026.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin and platform (1920); L-4 cab (1933, FireLookout.com doubts it was built); R-6 flat cab (1957)
facts.status_note: The R-6 cab was burned on the summit in 1975 after it could not be lifted off for removal. A hiker's account describes cement foundation blocks at the site.

access.note: WTA's trail note dated July 30, 2026 says the trail is closed until further notice because of the Little Giant Fire. No later notice was found.

visit.trail_note: Trail from the Lake Wenatchee Ranger Station trailhead, about four miles with 4,000 feet of gain per WTA (the Willhite guide gives 4.5 miles to the old site). Closed per the July 2026 WTA note. No tower remains to climb.

events.note: Camp set up on the summit as a heliograph lookout
Telephone line and trail built up the mountain to the lookout station
Harry T. Gisborne, a student from an eastern forestry school
D-6 cupola cabin and a platform installed
Ben S. Maxwell listed as lookout
Gladys West acted as relief lookout
Lawrence Cunningham was lookout on the peak
Lightning struck the station; flag pole shattered and some connections on a signal set burned. Sources differ on early 1929 versus a storm reported November 1929.
L-4 cab replaced the cupola per FFLOS and Willhite; FireLookout.com says photo evidence suggests it was not built
Mr. Ault employed as lookout; Mrs. Ault stayed at the peak part of the summer
R-6 flat cab replaced the L-4
Planned helicopter move to Alpine Lookout in June 1975 failed; the cab was burned to the ground on the summit. The guide reports a sixty-two-year lookout journal burned with it.
WTA trail note dated July 30, 2026: trail closed until further notice because of the Little Giant Fire

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 feet. The only 20-foot figure in the sources is a flag pole in the 1929 lightning account, not the lookout's height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and the Willhite guide say an L-4 cab replaced the cupola in 1933; FireLookout.com says photo evidence suggests it was not built. The story reports both views and does not pick one.
The Willhite guide dates the strike to early 1929. The Weebly page quotes a report dated November 1929 that describes a storm early in the season. Both are reported in the story.

The Willhite guide describes the trail as open without a closure note. WTA's note dated July 30, 2026 says the trail is closed until further notice. The later dated notice is used as the current access status.

sources.title: Dirty Face Peak - Lake Wenatchee Hikes

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on whether the 1933 L-4 cab was built, so the story reports both. The 1975 burn date is taken from the planned June 1975 removal and the R.I.P. dates on FireLookout.com; no source states the burn date outright. The height_m of 6.1 m in the record matches a 20-foot flag pole and has no source as a tower height. The WTA closure note is dated July 30, 2026; check whether the Little Giant Fire closure has been lifted before publishing. Must Hike Must Eat is an undated personal account, used only for the foundation blocks and the weather-monitoring use. Story is ~400 words.
